extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians preparing/submitting manuscripts to Selecta Mathematica
extracted.subtask_description: Author instructions and submission requirements for research articles submitted to the journal Selecta Mathematica (Birkhäuser / Springer). Covers authorship declarations, editorial process, manuscript format (LaTeX/base settings), figures, references, proof corrections, submission procedure, language editing, copyright, and open-access information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship / declarations on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies that the work described has not been published before; that it is not under consideration for publication elsewhere; that its publication has been approved by all coauthors, if any, as well as by the responsible authorities at the institute where the work has been carried out; that, if and when the manuscript is accepted for publication, the authors agree to automatically transfer the copyright to the publisher; and that the manuscript will not be published elsewhere in any language without the consent of the copyright holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are conditions of submission: ensure originality, exclusive consideration, coauthor and institutional approval, and acceptance of copyright transfer upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial process / submission acknowledgement and reprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be sent to the Editorial Office (selecta@math.mit.edu), these are acknowledged promptly following initial processing. Authors will be notified of the Editors' publishing decision once the refereeing process has been completed. Thirty reprints of published papers will be sent to the corresponding author free of charge. Additional reprints may be ordered from the Publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send manuscripts to the specified editorial email; expect prompt acknowledgement and notification after refereeing. Note the standard reprint policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred typesetting and no layout alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: To speed up publication, and to ensure a unified layout throughout the journal and to enhance the reliability of data, we strongly encourage the use of LATeX and its article style-file (10 pt.). AMSTeX, AMSLATEX and even Plain-TeX are also accepted, but not encouraged. We request that neither overfull nor underfull boxes be contained in the text, that equations not exceed the indicated text width, and that hyphenations as well as the page breaks be carefully checked. Apart from the following base commands, please do not change any default settings (e.g. no vertical or horizontal offsets). Please adhere as closely as possible to the mentioned guidelines. If you need some definitions of your own, please enclose these (and only these) into your document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal's LaTeX style (10pt) when possible. Avoid overfull/underfull h/v boxes, long equations exceeding text width, improper hyphenation and page breaks. Do not change default layout settings except allowed base commands; place any custom definitions explicitly and minimally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base layout settings (required defaults)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These base commands should be respected and other default settings should not be changed. Use these dimensions for consistent journal layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must include an abstract in English that summarizes the principle techniques and conclusions of the paper in relation to known results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an English abstract that explains main methods and conclusions and situates the work relative to known results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords and AMS subject classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords and where appropriate AMS subject classifications must accompany each article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include suitable keywords and AMS classification codes with the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated title / running head
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to indicate an abbreviated title, which will be used as a running head (no more than 50 characters including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short title ≤ 50 characters (including spaces) for use as the running head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and acceptable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be sent as: part of the document within a «picture» environment; EPS-files (encapsulated PostScript), with no reference to fonts which are not TeX, PostScript Base 35- or MathPifonts. Use the epsf.sty(.tex) to include these files into your document; TIFF (uncompressed) files; or fair copy on paper, whenever possible scaled to about 200%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed figures in the document or provide EPS (with allowable fonts) or uncompressed TIFF. If supplying paper copies, scale to ~200%. Use epsf.sty to include EPS files.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The literature should be referred to by numbers in the text in square brackets. In the bibliography, the references should be listed in alphabetical order or in order of appearance at the end of the manuscript. It should contain full article titles, chapter titles of books as well as first and last pages of each article. Standard abbreviations of journal names should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite references by numeric square brackets in text. Provide full bibliographic information (including article/chapter titles and page ranges). Order references alphabetically or by appearance. Use standard journal name abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and proof-stage changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of major changes made to the paper during the proof phase may be billed to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid major alterations at proof stage to prevent potential billing for correction costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure and subject line
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts should be sent to selecta@math.mit.edu with the subject 'new submission to Selecta'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified email and exact subject line for new submissions to ensure correct processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language editing and optional author services
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting your work in a well-structured manuscript and in well-written English gives it its best chance for editors and reviewers to understand it and evaluate it fairly. The experts at Springer Nature Author Services can help with manuscript preparation—including English language editing, developmental comments, manuscript formatting, figure preparation, translation, and more. You can also use our free Grammar Check tool for an evaluation of your work. Please note that using these tools, or any other service, is not a requirement for publication, nor does it imply or guarantee that editors will accept the article, or even select it for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider professional language/editing support if needed, but it is optional and does not influence editorial acceptance guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright by Birkhäuser / Springer Nature Switzerland AG
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted articles' copyright is held by the publisher; see the authorship declaration that authors agree to transfer copyright upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access information
rubrics_metrics.description: To find out more about publishing your work Open Access in Selecta Mathematica, including information on fees, funding and licences, visit our Open access publishing page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided Open Access page link for details on fees, funding, and licence options if you wish to publish open access.
